candidates.change_summary: Change return value from true to false.

Change return value to a bool constant true literal (same as original) is NOT distinct — skipped. Instead, replace return true with return !true; (i.e., false). Already covered. Move on. Replace return true with return _s; — but _s is out of scope. Replace return true with require(false) — but that would revert, breaking the requirement that both complete. Replace return true with return !false; still true. No distinct new value. Next: delete the require inside the call success check, so the call can fail silently. This changes behavior when call fails — it would not revert but return true. However, target says both complete (do not revert) and return different values. If a call fails in original, it reverts; in mutant, it completes and returns true. So that qualifies.

Remove the require(_s) check — already covered by delete of require(_s) block. Instead, move the return true inside the loop after the call but before the loop continues, so it returns after first iteration. This changes behavior when _tos.length > 1: original processes all addresses, mutant returns after first address.
